finding: The recommended setting ('Stop and let me review') blocks an ordinary government report.
evidence: R1 files run failed: Census P60-279 was flagged malformed_tables (19 tables) under the Balanced policy, so no file index was published. The free preview showed the same before any paid step.
impact: A user who uploads a normal statistical report with the defaults gets no index at all and must change a setting they do not understand.
next: Fix X2; until then make malformed tables a warning in Balanced.
after_fixes_evidence: A1 files run with 'Stop and let me review' published all three files; the Census report is no longer blocked (layout-ocr-v3).

finding: Borderless PDF tables lose their rows: whole columns are merged into one cell, and cells over 1,000 characters are cut.
evidence: Census Table A-1 (page 21): one cell holds '74,580 95,450 110,800 56,030 ...' with the row names in a different cell; 19 tables were cut at the 1,000-character cell limit. f2-q4 and f2-q5 missed in every round; the answer model declined f2-q4 in both v1 and v2.
impact: Values from report tables cannot be matched to their rows, so table questions on real reports fail or are declined; data past the cut is lost.
next: New extractor version: detect merged-column tables (cells with many line-separated values) and fall back to text lines for those tables instead of truncating.
after_fixes_evidence: f2-q4 and f2-q5 now retrieve their Table A-1 row (rank 2 and 4; before: not in the top 5). f2-q4 answer changed from wrongly declined to correct ($110,800). Rotated landscape tables are kept whole but transposed (known limit).

finding: 'Publish the other files and show warnings' does not publish the others when a file cannot be read.
evidence: R3b (OCR off) with warn-v1: the scanned report had no text, and the whole files run failed instead of excluding it. warn-v1 only excludes files marked optional.
impact: The plain-language choice in the Extract panel promises more than it does.
next: Either exclude any unreadable file under this choice, or reword it to match the behaviour.
after_fixes_evidence: Covered by PostgreSQL tests for files, S3 and Website runs: an unreadable item is skipped and the rest publish. Not re-run live: no A1 item failed.

finding: Website tables are flattened to one value per line.
evidence: GOV.UK minimum-wage and vehicle-tax tables and the Wikipedia infobox appear as single values on separate lines; the column a value belongs to is lost. No website chunk is stored as a table.
impact: Answers that depend on a column can go wrong; in this test the model still answered the three website table questions correctly.
next: Render HTML tables as Markdown rows in the website extractor (new web extractor version).
after_fixes_evidence: A1 website index has 156 table chunks, all with a header row (R1: 0).

finding: Line-break de-hyphenation merges real hyphenated words.
evidence: 'married-\ncouple' in the Census report became 'marriedcouple' after Clean.
impact: Search for the hyphenated term and exact quotes can miss.
next: Keep the hyphen when both parts are dictionary words or the hyphen is followed by a lowercase word that also appears hyphenated elsewhere.
after_fixes_evidence: 4 of 5 'married-couple' occurrences in the Census report keep their hyphen; one still reads 'marriedcouple' (cause not yet traced).

finding: On long Wikipedia articles the lead paragraph can rank below notes and references.
evidence: w2-q2 (reef count) and w2-q6 (Moon distance) found the right page but not the lead chunk in R1; references and explanatory notes are indexed.
impact: Lower rank for the most important facts on long pages.
next: Consider excluding reference lists and footnotes from website chunks.
after_fixes_evidence: No chunk from a References/Notes/External links section and no 'Retrieved ...' citation text in the A1 website index.

finding: Website run details list out-of-scope links as succeeded with 0 chunks, often twice.
evidence: The Python crawl reports 56 items, including changelog, genindex and licence pages outside /3/tutorial/; only the 17 tutorial pages were indexed.
impact: Run details look as if unwanted pages were ingested.
next: Show discovered-but-out-of-scope links as excluded with a reason, once each.
after_fixes_evidence: PostgreSQL test: an out-of-scope link found twice is listed once as excluded/skipped. A1 reused the R1 snapshot, so no new crawl links were listed.

finding: Embedding cost is not recorded by the app.
evidence: Ingestion runs and indexes have no cost field; this test used an upper-bound estimate from indexed bytes.
impact: Indexing cost shows as unknown in the product.
next: Record provider-reported embedding tokens and cost per run.
after_fixes_evidence: The app recorded provider-reported embedding usage: websites 137,559 tokens / $0.0028; files 0 tokens / $0 (every vector reused).

finding: A combined citation such as [S1, S2] is recorded as invalid, so the answer shows no valid citation.
evidence: A1: w1-q1, f2-q4, f2-q6, f3-q1 cite '[S1, S2]'-style groups and have valid=[]; R1 shows the same (w1-q1, w4-q4). validate_citations() treats the whole bracket as one label.
impact: Correct, supported answers look uncited in the evidence view.
next: Split a bracket on commas before checking labels; add a test.
after_fixes_evidence: Found during the spec 0007 re-run; not part of spec 0007.
